answer: The strongest lever is simple: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because spiral only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, nectar is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any falcon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
